messages:
Harper (Hiring): Quick heads-up  Riley is relocating from SF to NYC for the machine learning integration role on June 15 and will be working from a client site in Manhattan. Riley is on H-1B currently approved for bay area location. Do we need an amendment/LCA?
Jules (People Ops): Likely yes if the new NYC site is outside the approved L-geo area. We need immigration to confirm. Also this triggers state tax and payroll withholding changes, and we should prepare the 10-business-day worksite notice posting.
Priya (Immigration Counsel): Confirmed: moving Riley to a new metropolitan statistical area constitutes a material change to worksite and requires a new LCA (ETA-9035) and H-1B amended petition (I-129). Employer must post LCA notice at the new worksite for 10 business days and keep proof of posting. We can file the amended petition; processing time varies. If you want faster, we can request premium processing but cost + USCIS times apply.
Riley (Candidate): If you file amendment, can I start at the NYC client site while it's pending? Id like to avoid gaps.
Priya (Immigration Counsel): Conservative approach: do not start at the new worksite until we file the LCA and ideally the amendment is filed. Some employers wait until the I-129 is filed (not necessarily approved) before allowing the move; others wait for approval. There's risk with starting before filing  USCIS expects compliance. We recommend filing LCA immediately and filing the amendment petition before Riley reports onsite. If you need Riley onsite urgently, consider remote support or temporary co-working at SF until LCA filed.
Sam (Payroll): Payroll/tax notes: moving employee to NY means NY state withholding and possible NYC local tax, and unemployment insurance registration if substantial headcount there. Need Rileys NY address, new W-4 state form, and adjust payroll location by the first run after start. Also accruals for paid time off remain as-is but some policies consider state law differences. Give payroll at least 7 business days to change state tax profile.
Claire (Benefits): Benefits won't be affected by state change for medical, but commuter/transportation benefits and some voluntary insurance rates may differ by state. If Riley changes address, beneficiary/benefit notices need update. No break in coverage if payroll continues uninterrupted.
Nico (Office Manager): For LCA posting we need a pinned physical notice at the client site; will coordinate with client facilities. If client restricts postings, we can post at nearest Redwood office and on internal employee intranet; well also gather affidavits from facility manager as proof. Need exact site address and start date to prepare the posting.
Jules (People Ops): Action items: 1) Harper/Riley: confirm exact NYC worksite address and planned first onsite date. 2) Priya: file LCA (ETA-9035) and prepare I-129 amendment draft. 3) Nico: coordinate physical and intranet posting. 4) Sam: prep payroll/state-change checklist and timeline. 5) Claire: check commuter plan options for NY and update benefits record.
Harper (Hiring): Rileys client site: 101 Park Ave, Manhattan. Planned onsite first day July 1. Riley can continue remote SF work until then.
Priya (Immigration Counsel): I'll start LCA prep today. Once LCA is certified we will file amended I-129; if you want faster we can do premium processing. Estimated timeline: LCA cert 7-10 business days if no issues; I-129 amended petition processing standard ~2-6 months, premium ~15 calendar days. We recommend filing LCA this week to meet July 1 target for filing I-129 before onsite start.
Riley (Candidate): Ok remote till July 1 is fine. Please let me know what docs you need from me.
Priya (Immigration Counsel): Need Rileys current passport copy, most recent H-1B approval (I-797), signed offer letter, job duties summary for NY role, and salary confirmation (NY pay will be same). Also confirm whether theres a material change in duties or pay that might require wage determination update.
Sam (Payroll): For tax setup send NY home address and expected payroll move date. Riley, we'll need an updated state W-4 and bank details if anything changes. Also note: NYC does not have a separate city income tax like NYC resident tax, but there is locality depending on municipality  we'll confirm.
Nico (Office Manager): I'll confirm with client facilities about posting permission and parking access. If client says no physical posting allowed, we'll document our attempts and post at nearest Redwood-designated worksite + intranet copy. Keep records.
Jules (People Ops): Also adding a brief template for employee notice wording so legal signing is consistent. We'll need to keep a copy in Riley's case file.
Priya (Immigration Counsel): One more operational note: USCIS sometimes asks for proof of LCA posting during an H-1B site visit or RFE. Keep screenshots of intranet posting, date-stamped photo of notice at site, and signed acknowledgement if client provides. We'll also draft an employer cover memo.
Harper (Hiring): Great  timeline looks doable. Priya, ping when LCA is filed and Sam/Nico will take over logistics.
Priya (Immigration Counsel): Will do. Filing LCA today; will post certified LCA copy here and confirm when I-129 is filed. If Harper wants premium, we need approval for cost center.
Jules (People Ops): I'll prep a short internal comms snippet for Rileys team re: location change and timing. Also logging this under "h1b-amendments" candidate tag.
Sam (Payroll): Noted. I'll provisionally adjust payroll flags for NY effective first payroll after July 1 and send Riley the state W-4 link.
Riley (Candidate): Thanks team  appreciate the clarity. I'll upload passport and I-797 tonight.
Priya (Immigration Counsel): Received docs expected tonight. I'll update the thread when LCA submitted.
